intent.raw_query: Tokyo city break, $3000 for couple, food and tech culture, April 2026 from SFO

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the iconic Tsukiji Outer Market and sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from local vendors. Engage with fishmongers and food artisans who have been operating for generations, offering an authentic taste of Tokyo's legendary food culture.

experiences.name: Odaiba Waterfront Tech & Culture Day
experiences.description: Visit Odaiba, Tokyo's futuristic man-made island on Tokyo Bay, combining beachfront access at Odaiba Beach with visits to teamLab Borderless digital art museum and the Toyota Mega Web tech showcase. Experience cutting-edge Japanese innovation with stunning waterfront views of Rainbow Bridge.

experiences.name: Asakusa Traditional Culture Walk
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in old Tokyo at Senso-ji Temple, stroll through Nakamise Shopping Street for traditional crafts and snacks, and witness local rituals and festivals. Dress in a rented kimono for an authentic cultural experience in Tokyo's most historic district.

experiences.name: Akihabara Electric Town Deep Dive
experiences.description: Explore the world-famous electronics and anime hub of Akihabara, visiting multi-floor gadget stores, retro game shops, and maid cafes. Discover the latest in Japanese consumer tech, robotics demos, and the vibrant otaku subculture that defines modern Tokyo's tech identity.

experiences.name: Shiodome & Hamarikyu Waterfront Food & Garden Experience
experiences.description: Visit the stunning Hamarikyu Gardens, a historic tidal garden on Tokyo Bay, followed by a traditional matcha tea ceremony in the garden's teahouse. Conclude with a dinner cruise along the Sumida River sampling kaiseki-style Japanese cuisine with illuminated city views from the water.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Tokyo, Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Narita Express (N'EX) or Airport Limousine Bus to Tsukiji area. Budget tip: N'EX to Shinjuku then transfer is ~¥3,070; IC card (Suica/Pasmo) recommended.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Tsukiji, Chuo City Boutique Stay. Once settled, take a short walk to explore the Tsukiji Outer Market — browse fresh seafood stalls, tamagoyaki shops, and street snacks. Even in the afternoon many vendors are still open. Pick up a cheap snack like a grilled scallop or tamagoyaki skewer (¥200–400).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Sumida River waterfront near Tsukiji for sunset views. Head to Hamarikyu Gardens entrance area for a peaceful evening walk (gardens close at 17:00, so admire from outside). Dinner in the Tsukiji Outer Market neighborhood at one of the casual sushi or donburi restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a convenience store onigiri (¥120–200) at the airport arrivals hall
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or on the train — convenience store bento (¥500–700)
meals.dinner: Tsukiji Outer Market area — try a seafood donburi bowl at a local shop like Tsukiji Shrimp or similar casual eatery (¥800–1,200)

day_by_day.notes: Buy a Suica IC card at the airport for seamless train and bus travel throughout the trip. Load ¥3,000–5,000 initially. Keep receipts to track daily spending. April weather is spring — bring a light jacket as evenings can be cool (10–18°C range typical).

day_by_day.morning: Early visit to Tsukiji Outer Market for a classic Japanese breakfast — fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, or a bowl of clam miso soup. Markets are liveliest 7:00–10:00. Browse the narrow lanes packed with seafood, knives, and cooking goods. Free to explore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short subway ride to Ginza (adjacent to Tsukiji) and explore the free-entry sections — window shop the luxury district, visit the free Itoya stationery flagship store (9 floors of beautiful Japanese stationery and design goods). Then head to the Sony Building area and nearby free tech showrooms. Walk through Hibiya Park (free entry) nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Take the subway to Akihabara (Electric Town) — Tokyo's iconic tech and anime culture hub. Explore the multi-story electronics stores like Yodobashi Akiba and Bic Camera (free to browse). Walk the main street lined with neon signs and retro game shops. Dinner in Akihabara.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — tamagoyaki on a stick + clam miso soup (¥400–600)
meals.lunch: Ginza area convenience store or a standing soba/ramen shop (¥600–900)
meals.dinner: Akihabara — try a curry rice chain like CoCo Ichibanya or a ramen shop (¥700–1,000)

day_by_day.notes: Ginza's high-end stores are free to enter and browse. Many electronics stores in Akihabara offer tax-free shopping for tourists — bring your passport. Akihabara is best experienced in the evening when the neon lights are fully lit.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa (free entry, opens at 6:00). Arrive early to beat crowds and experience the serene atmosphere. Walk through Nakamise Shopping Street for affordable traditional souvenirs — fans, tenugui towels, ningyo-yaki cakes (¥100–300 each).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ueno Park (free entry) — stroll through the park, visit the Ueno Zoo if interested (¥600 entry) or simply enjoy the park's ponds and temples for free. In mid-April cherry blossom season may still be lingering. Visit the free outdoor areas around Tokyo National Museum grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ameyoko Market in Ueno — a lively outdoor market street with cheap street food, clothing, and goods. Great for budget shopping and snacking. Grab yakitori skewers or takoyaki from stalls. Return to Tsukiji by subway.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store near hotel or grab a ningyo-yaki pastry at Nakamise (¥200–400)
meals.lunch: Ueno Park area — buy bento from a convenience store and picnic in the park (¥500–700)
meals.dinner: Ameyoko Market — street food crawl: takoyaki, yakitori, gyoza (¥600–1,000 total)

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is Tokyo's most visited temple — arriving before 8:00 AM ensures a quieter, more authentic experience. Ueno Park is free and beautiful in spring. Ameyoko is one of Tokyo's best budget food and shopping streets — bargaining is acceptable at some stalls.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Harajuku — visit Meiji Jingu Shrine (free entry, opens at sunrise). Walk the forested path through the shrine grounds for a peaceful contrast to the city. The forested approach takes about 10 minutes each way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down Takeshita Street in Harajuku — Tokyo's famous youth fashion street packed with quirky shops, crepe stands, and pop culture. Explore Omotesando (the 'Champs-Élysées of Tokyo') for free architecture viewing. Visit the free Omotesando Hills atrium. Then head to Shibuya — walk to the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing and observe from street level (free).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Shibuya's budget-friendly izakayas and food stalls around Nonbei Yokocho (Whiskey Alley) and Shibuya Center-gai. Enjoy the vibrant nightlife atmosphere. Return to Tsukiji via subway.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store near hotel — onigiri + green tea (¥300–500)
meals.lunch: Harajuku Takeshita Street — crepe (¥500–700) or cheap ramen nearby
meals.dinner: Shibuya — try a budget izakaya set meal with draft beer (¥1,000–1,500) or a gyudon (beef bowl) at Yoshinoya/Matsuya (¥400–600)

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is serene and free — a must-visit for cultural immersion. Shibuya Scramble is best experienced at peak evening hours when thousands cross simultaneously. Avoid sitting-down restaurants in Omotesando as prices are high — stick to standing bars or chains.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic artificial island. Take the Yurikamome monorail from Shimbashi (scenic ride, ~¥330) for views of Rainbow Bridge and Tokyo Bay. Explore teamLab Borderless digital art museum (book in advance, ~¥3,200) — a world-renowned immersive tech art experience perfectly aligned with tech culture interests.
day_by_day.afternoon: After teamLab, explore Odaiba's free outdoor areas: the Statue of Liberty replica, Odaiba Seaside Park (free), and the futuristic architecture of the Fuji TV Building (exterior free). Browse DiverCity Tokyo Plaza's free Gundam statue (1:1 scale RX-78 Gundam replica) — iconic for tech/anime culture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Tokyo via the Yurikamome or water bus (Tokyo Cruise from Odaiba to Hinode Pier, ~¥480). Enjoy dinner near Tsukiji or at a local neighborhood spot.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area convenience store — coffee + pastry (¥300–400)
meals.lunch: Odaiba — Aqua City Odaiba food court has affordable options like ramen or udon (¥700–1,000)
meals.dinner: Near Tsukiji — a local teishoku (set meal) restaurant for a balanced meal (¥800–1,200)

day_by_day.notes: Book teamLab Borderless tickets online in advance — it often sells out, especially on weekends. The water bus back from Odaiba is a scenic and affordable alternative to the monorail and gives great views of the Tokyo skyline at dusk.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Yanaka — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) neighborhoods. Walk the Yanaka Ginza shopping street, browse vintage shops, and visit the historic Yanaka Cemetery (free, beautiful in spring). This area offers a rare glimpse of pre-war Tokyo atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Nezu Shrine (free entry) — a beautiful Shinto shrine with hundreds of torii gates similar to Kyoto's Fushimi Inari but far less crowded. Walk through the torii tunnel and explore the shrine grounds. Then head to Nishi-Nippori for rooftop views of the Yanaka area from the Scai the Bathhouse gallery area (free exterior).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Koenji or Shimokitazawa (Tokyo's indie/subculture hubs) for an evening of browsing vintage clothing stores and listening to live music at small budget venues. Return to Tsukiji.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka Ginza — fresh croquette or melon bread from a local bakery (¥150–300)
meals.lunch: Yanaka area — a local soba shop or retro kissaten (coffee shop) lunch set (¥700–1,000)
meals.dinner: Shimokitazawa — a budget curry or ramen shop popular with students (¥700–1,000)

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is one of the most culturally rich and budget-friendly neighborhoods in Tokyo — nearly everything is free to explore. Nezu Shrine's torii gates are stunning and far less crowded than Kyoto's equivalent. Shimokitazawa is Tokyo's bohemian heart — great for evening atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building in Shinjuku for a free observation deck (open from 9:00, free entry) — panoramic 360° views of Tokyo including Mt. Fuji on clear days. Then explore Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (¥500 entry) — one of Tokyo's most beautiful parks, especially in spring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore East Shinjuku — walk through the Golden Gai area (tiny alley bars, fascinating to explore even during the day), Kabukicho entertainment district, and the free Samurai Museum area (exterior). Browse Disk Union (multi-floor music store) and Kinokuniya bookstore for free browsing.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the legendary Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) in West Shinjuku — a narrow alley of tiny yakitori restaurants with just a few seats each. Smoky, atmospheric, and very authentic. Budget-friendly skewers and cold beer under the train tracks.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store near hotel (¥300–500)
meals.lunch: Shinjuku Gyoen — buy a bento from a nearby convenience store and picnic in the garden (¥500–700)
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho — yakitori skewers + beer (¥1,000–1,500 total for a satisfying meal)

day_by_day.notes: The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck is completely free — one of the best views in the city without paying for a sky tower. Shinjuku Gyoen is excellent for a peaceful afternoon. Omoide Yokocho is cash-only at most stalls — bring yen.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shiodome and the Hamarikyu Gardens (¥300 entry) — a beautiful traditional Japanese garden with a tidal pond, right next to Tsukiji. Enjoy a traditional matcha tea ceremony at the garden's teahouse (¥500 additional). This is a peaceful morning activity very close to your hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Nihonbashi area (walking distance from Tsukiji) — visit the historic Nihonbashi Bridge (Japan's kilometer zero), browse the Coredo Muromachi shopping complex, and visit the free Mitsui Memorial Museum lobby. Walk to the Bank of Japan building (free exterior viewing) for Meiji-era architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Kanda/Jimbocho — Tokyo's famous used bookstore district. Browse hundreds of shops selling manga, vintage books, and ukiyo-e prints. Many shops are open until 20:00. Dinner in the area at an affordable local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh morning sushi set (¥800–1,200) — treat yourself to the classic experience
meals.lunch: Nihonbashi — standing sushi bar or a tempura tendon set (¥800–1,100)
meals.dinner: Jimbocho/Kanda — a hearty curry rice at a local curry shop (¥700–900)

day_by_day.notes: Hamarikyu Gardens is a hidden gem right next to your hotel — surprisingly quiet and beautiful. The matcha tea in the traditional teahouse overlooking the pond is a culturally rich experience for a very low cost. Jimbocho is paradise for culture lovers — even browsing is free.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (about 2 hours from Asakusa via Tobu Nikko Line — budget ~¥1,360 one way). Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Tosho-gu Shrine complex — ornate shrines and mausoleums surrounded by ancient cedar forests. Entry to the main complex is ¥1,300.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko — walk to Rinno-ji Temple (¥400), see the famous Shinkyo Sacred Bridge (free to view, ¥300 to walk across), and hike along the forested paths. The area is stunning in spring with fresh greenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Arrive back at Tsukiji by 19:00–20:00. Light dinner near the hotel after a long day of travel.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store before departure — onigiri + coffee (¥300–500)
meals.lunch: Nikko — yuba (tofu skin) cuisine is the local specialty; try a yuba soba set at a local restaurant (¥900–1,200)
meals.dinner: Near Tsukiji hotel — simple ramen or gyudon (¥600–900)

day_by_day.notes: Buy a Tobu Nikko Pass for unlimited rides and discounts (¥2,780 from Asakusa, 2-day pass). Start early — aim to leave Asakusa by 7:30 AM to maximize time in Nikko. Wear comfortable walking shoes as Nikko involves significant walking and some steps.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Akihabara again — this time with a focus on tech culture deep dive. Explore the upper floors of Yodobashi Akiba (8 floors of electronics, gaming, and tech). Visit the free Gundam Café area and browse retro game shops for vintage Famicom/Super Famicom cartridges. Check out the free Akihabara Radio Kaikan building floors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the National Museum of Nature and Science in Ueno (¥630 entry) — excellent exhibits on technology, science, and Japanese innovation. Then visit the nearby Tokyo National Museum (¥1,000) for world-class Japanese art and cultural artifacts if time allows — or choose one museum.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Kagurazaka — a charming French-Japanese neighborhood with cobblestone alleys (yokocho), traditional restaurants, and a unique cultural blend. Walk the narrow Geisha alley lanes and enjoy the atmospheric evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area convenience store (¥300–500)
meals.lunch: Akihabara — a maid café experience for lunch (budget ¥1,000–1,500 for food + cover charge) — unique Tokyo tech culture experience
meals.dinner: Kagurazaka — a traditional Japanese kaiseki-lite set meal at a mid-range restaurant or affordable French bistro (¥1,000–1,500)

day_by_day.notes: Maid cafés in Akihabara are a quintessential Tokyo tech/pop culture experience — prices are reasonable for a one-time visit. The National Museum of Nature and Science has English audio guides available. Kagurazaka is best explored slowly on foot in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab Planets in Toyosu (if not already visited — different from Borderless; tickets ~¥3,200). A stunning immersive digital art installation with water rooms and floating gardens. Book tickets in advance online. Toyosu is also home to the Toyosu Market (replaced Tsukiji's wholesale market) — the outer observation decks are free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Kiyosumi-Shirakawa neighborhood — Tokyo's specialty coffee culture hub. Walk between artisan coffee roasters (Allpress Espresso, Blue Bottle Coffee Japan's original location) for affordable specialty coffee (¥500–700 per cup). Browse the area's art galleries and quiet streets.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Roppongi for the evening — visit Mori Art Museum (¥2,000 entry, open until 22:00 on weekends) for contemporary art with panoramic city views from the 52nd floor included. Roppongi Hills area is free to walk through and impressive at night.

meals.breakfast: Kiyosumi-Shirakawa specialty coffee + pastry (¥700–900)
meals.lunch: Toyosu area — fresh seafood bowl at the Toyosu Market outer market restaurants (¥1,000–1,500)
meals.dinner: Roppongi — budget-friendly option: a conveyor belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) chain like Sushiro or Kura Sushi (¥800–1,200)

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Planets is a different experience from Borderless — both are worth visiting if budget allows. Kiyosumi-Shirakawa is a very local, less touristy neighborhood perfect for experiencing Tokyo's modern food culture. Mori Art Museum's city views alone are worth the entry price.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum in Ryogoku (¥600 entry) — a fascinating museum covering the history of Tokyo from the Edo period to modern times with life-size reconstructions of old streets, bridges, and buildings. Culturally rich and very affordable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Ryogoku Kokugikan Sumo Arena — even if there's no tournament, the sumo museum inside is free. Walk the area around the arena where sumo stables are located — you may see sumo wrestlers walking the streets in the early afternoon. Then explore the Kiyosumi Gardens (¥150 entry) for a quiet afternoon stroll.
day_by_day.evening: Final big night out — head to Shibuya or Shinjuku for a farewell dinner at a proper izakaya. Enjoy a multi-course izakaya experience with small plates, yakitori, edamame, and Japanese craft beer or sake. Soak in the lively atmosphere of a Tokyo Friday night.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — final morning market breakfast: sushi or tamagoyaki (¥500–800)
meals.lunch: Ryogoku — chanko nabe (sumo wrestlers' hot pot stew) at a local chanko restaurant is the local specialty (¥1,000–1,500)
meals.dinner: Shibuya/Shinjuku izakaya — all-you-can-drink + food set if available (¥2,000–2,500 for a full evening)

day_by_day.notes: Check the Grand Sumo Tournament schedule before your trip — if a basho (tournament) is held in April in Tokyo, tickets can be purchased for as little as ¥2,200 for upper seats. Chanko nabe in Ryogoku is a must-try local specialty — many restaurants near the arena serve it affordably.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for one final Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast — enjoy the market one last time and pick up any last-minute food souvenirs: vacuum-packed dashi packets, wasabi, or matcha. Browse the knife shops for a quality Japanese kitchen knife as a durable souvenir.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel. Store luggage at the hotel or a coin locker at a nearby station (¥300–600). Take a final walk along the Sumida River or through Hamarikyu Gardens if time permits. Head to the airport via N'EX or Airport Limousine Bus — allow 90–120 minutes travel time plus check-in time.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Enjoy duty-free shopping at the airport for last-minute gifts — Japanese Kit Kat flavors, sake, and snacks are popular and reasonably priced at airport shops.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — final sushi breakfast or tamagoyaki (¥500–800)
meals.lunch: Airport terminal — try a proper airport ramen or soba before departure (¥900–1,300)
meals.dinner: On the plane

day_by_day.notes: Return your Suica IC card at the airport for a refund of remaining balance (minus ¥220 handling fee) — or keep it for future Japan trips as it never expires. Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before international departure. Pack any liquid food purchases (sauces, etc.) in checked luggage.

trip_options.title: Classic Tokyo, Japan Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – In transit. Flight LH arrives at Narita/Haneda at 13:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at airport at 13:00. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and take the Narita Express or Airport Limousine Bus to Tsukiji/Chuo City (~60–90 min). Check into your Tsukiji boutique hotel, freshen up, and take a gentle orientation stroll around the Tsukiji Outer Market neighborhood to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Ease into Tokyo with a relaxed walk along the Sumida River waterfront near Tsukiji. Visit the lively Tsukiji Outer Market area for an early dinner – explore the small stalls and specialty shops still open in the early evening.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport (ramen or soba at an airport restaurant, ~¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tsukiji Outer Market – try a fresh seafood bowl (kaisendon) or grilled skewers from one of the local stalls (~¥1,500–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Jet lag tip: Stay awake until at least 21:00 local time to help reset your body clock. Keep Day 1 light. Buy a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for seamless transit throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day properly at Tsukiji Outer Market – arrive by 08:00 for the freshest experience. Browse the stalls selling tamagoyaki (sweet egg omelette), fresh sushi, pickles, and seafood snacks. This is the authentic local food experience Tokyo is famous for.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to nearby Hamarikyu Gardens (15-min walk) – a stunning traditional Japanese garden with a tidal pond and teahouse, framed by skyscrapers. Take the scenic water bus from Hamarikyu up the Sumida River to Asakusa (~40 min, ¥1,040). Explore Senso-ji Temple, Tokyo's oldest and most iconic temple, and the Nakamise shopping street.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Asakusa for the evening. Explore the backstreets of Kappabashi (Kitchenware Town) if still open, then enjoy dinner in Asakusa. Walk along the Sumida River for illuminated views of the Skytree at night.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast – fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and clam miso soup (~¥1,500–¥2,000)
meals.lunch: Lunch at Hamarikyu Garden teahouse or a nearby soba restaurant (~¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Asakusa dinner at a traditional tempura restaurant such as Daikokuya Tempura (~¥2,000–¥3,000)

day_by_day.notes: Hamarikyu Gardens entry fee: ¥300. Senso-ji is free to enter. The Sumida River water bus is a scenic and practical way to travel between the two areas.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Akihabara (Electric Town) – Tokyo's legendary hub for tech culture, anime, manga, and electronics. Spend the morning exploring multi-floor electronics stores like Yodobashi Camera and Akihabara Radio Center. Browse retro game shops, gadget stores, and cutting-edge tech displays.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dive deeper into Akihabara's tech culture: visit the Akihabara UDX building and explore the maid café culture (try a themed café experience if curious). Then head to the nearby 3331 Arts Chiyoda, a creative arts and tech space housed in a former school. Walk to Kanda Myojin Shrine, which has a fascinating connection to tech and game culture (IT companies pray here for digital success).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ginza (20-min subway from Akihabara) for a sophisticated evening. Window-shop along Chuo-dori, then enjoy dinner at one of Ginza's mid-range restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local kissaten (Japanese coffee shop) near Tsukiji (~¥500–¥1,000)
meals.lunch: Akihabara lunch – try a popular curry chain like CoCo Ichibanya or a ramen shop (~¥900–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Ginza dinner at a mid-range Japanese izakaya or a tonkatsu restaurant (~¥2,500–¥3,500)

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best explored on foot. Many electronics and game shops open around 10:00–11:00. Maid café experiences typically cost ¥500–¥1,000 for a drink plus a service charge – check menus before entering.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shibuya – start with the world-famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing. Head up to the Shibuya Sky observation deck on top of Shibuya Scramble Square for panoramic 360° views of Tokyo (book tickets in advance, ¥2,000). Explore the surrounding streets and the Shibuya Stream area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short train ride to Harajuku. Stroll down Takeshita Street for quirky youth fashion and crepes. Then explore the more upscale Omotesando boulevard – Tokyo's Champs-Élysées – lined with flagship stores and impressive architecture. Visit the Omotesando Hills shopping complex designed by Tadao Ando.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shinjuku for the evening. Explore the neon-lit Kabukicho entertainment district, the Golden Gai alleyways (dozens of tiny atmospheric bars), and the lively Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) for yakitori skewers under the train tracks.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast (7-Eleven or FamilyMart near Tsukiji – onigiri, coffee, pastry, ~¥400–¥700)
meals.lunch: Harajuku crepe and snacks on Takeshita Street, or a café lunch on Omotesando (~¥1,000–¥1,800)
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) in Shinjuku – grilled yakitori skewers and cold beer in a tiny atmospheric stall (~¥2,000–¥3,000)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is busy in Shibuya and Harajuku – expect crowds. Shibuya Sky tickets should be pre-booked online. Golden Gai bars are very small (5–8 seats) and some charge a table fee (¥500–¥1,000) – check before sitting.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Meiji Jingu Shrine in Harajuku – a serene forested Shinto shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji, offering a peaceful contrast to the urban energy. Arrive early (~09:00) for the calmest atmosphere. Walk the long forested path to the main shrine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the train to Yanaka – one of Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) neighborhoods that survived WWII bombing. Explore Yanaka Ginza shopping street, browse antique shops, pottery studios, and local galleries. Visit Yanaka Cemetery, a beautiful and historic green space popular during cherry blossom season.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ueno for the evening. Explore Ameyoko Market – a bustling open-air market street near Ueno Station. Browse food stalls, clothing, and imported goods. Enjoy dinner in the Ueno area.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a traditional kissaten (Japanese-style coffee shop) near Harajuku (~¥700–¥1,200)
meals.lunch: Yanaka Ginza street food – try menchi katsu (fried minced meat cutlet) and local snacks (~¥800–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Ueno Ameyoko area – try an izakaya or a Chinese-Japanese fusion restaurant in the Ueno backstreets (~¥2,000–¥3,000)

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is free to enter. Yanaka is best explored slowly on foot – wear comfortable shoes. The neighborhood is especially photogenic with its traditional wooden buildings and old-fashioned atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab Planets or teamLab Borderless (check which is open in 2027 – teamLab Borderless is scheduled to reopen in Azabudai Hills). This world-renowned digital art museum blends technology, interactivity, and immersive culture – a perfect intersection of tech and art. Book tickets well in advance (¥3,200–¥4,500).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Azabudai Hills development (one of Tokyo's newest mega-projects) or head to nearby Roppongi. Visit the Mori Art Museum at Roppongi Hills (contemporary art with city views from the 53rd floor, ~¥2,000). Walk through the Roppongi Art Triangle area.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Roppongi or head to nearby Hiroo/Nishi-Azabu for dinner. The area has excellent mid-range international and Japanese dining options. Return to Tsukiji by subway.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a neighborhood café near Tsukiji (~¥600–¥1,000)
meals.lunch: Café or restaurant within or near the teamLab venue (~¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Roppongi or Nishi-Azabu – try a stylish Japanese restaurant or an izakaya with creative small plates (~¥3,000–¥4,000)

day_by_day.notes: teamLab tickets must be booked online in advance – they sell out quickly. Wear comfortable clothes and be prepared to remove shoes at teamLab Planets. Check venue operating hours closer to your travel date.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (about 2 hours from Tokyo by Tobu Nikko Line from Asakusa, or Shinkansen + local train). Nikko is a UNESCO World Heritage Site with ornate Tosho-gu Shrine, surrounded by cedar forests and mountain scenery. Explore the elaborate shrine complex.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko – visit Rinnoji Temple, the Yomeimon Gate (one of Japan's most decorated gates), and the Shinkyo Sacred Bridge over the Daiya River. If time permits, walk toward Kegon Falls (one of Japan's top waterfalls).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo in the early evening (arrive back ~18:00–19:00). Enjoy a quiet dinner near the hotel in Tsukiji to rest after the day trip.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast before departure (~¥400–¥700)
meals.lunch: Nikko yuba (tofu skin) cuisine – a local specialty. Try a set meal at a restaurant near the shrines (~¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.dinner: Tsukiji area dinner – a quiet local restaurant or sushi bar near the hotel (~¥2,000–¥3,000)

day_by_day.notes: Round-trip Tobu Nikko Line from Asakusa: ~¥2,700 (limited express). Alternatively, use the Nikko Pass for unlimited travel (~¥4,520). Nikko Tosho-gu entry: ~¥1,300. Start early (depart by 07:30–08:00) to maximize time at the site.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Odaiba – Tokyo's futuristic artificial island in Tokyo Bay. Take the scenic Yurikamome monorail from Shimbashi Station (great views of Rainbow Bridge). Visit the teamLab or Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation) – a world-class science and tech museum with interactive exhibits on AI, robotics, and space (~¥630).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue in Odaiba – visit DiverCity Tokyo Plaza and see the life-size Gundam statue (a must for tech/anime fans). Explore the Palette Town area or the Toyota Mega Web (if still operating). Walk along the Odaiba beachfront with views of Rainbow Bridge and the Tokyo skyline.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Tokyo via the Yurikamome monorail or water bus. Head to Shiodome or Shimbashi for dinner. The Caretta Shiodome complex has good mid-range dining options with views.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a Tsukiji local café or bakery (~¥600–¥1,000)
meals.lunch: Odaiba – try a ramen restaurant or food court in DiverCity or Aqua City (~¥1,000–¥1,800)
meals.dinner: Shiodome or Shimbashi – izakaya dinner or a Japanese set meal restaurant (~¥2,500–¥3,500)

day_by_day.notes: Miraikan is excellent for tech culture enthusiasts – allow at least 2–3 hours. The Yurikamome monorail offers spectacular views; sit at the front for the best vantage point. Odaiba is a ~20-min monorail ride from Shimbashi.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno – Japan's largest and oldest museum, housing an extraordinary collection of Japanese art, samurai armor, ceramics, and Buddhist sculpture. The main Honkan building alone is worth 2–3 hours (~¥1,000 general admission).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the rest of Ueno Park – visit the Ueno Zoo (optional, ¥600) or the National Museum of Western Art (Le Corbusier-designed, UNESCO listed). Then head to Koenji or Shimokitazawa by train – two of Tokyo's most characterful bohemian neighborhoods known for vintage shops, independent cafés, and live music venues.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Shimokitazawa for the evening – explore the winding backstreet alleys filled with vintage clothing stores, record shops, and small live music bars. Enjoy dinner at one of the neighborhood's charming local restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Ueno area café or a traditional Japanese breakfast set at a nearby restaurant (~¥700–¥1,200)
meals.lunch: Museum café at Tokyo National Museum or a nearby restaurant in Ueno (~¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Shimokitazawa – a cozy local curry restaurant, ramen shop, or a small izakaya (~¥1,500–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo National Museum is closed on Mondays. Shimokitazawa is beloved by locals for its anti-chain-store, independent spirit. The neighborhood is best explored slowly and spontaneously – don't over-plan this evening.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum (or Edo-Tokyo Open Air Architectural Museum in Koganei if the main museum is still under renovation in 2027). This museum offers a deep dive into Tokyo's history from the Edo period to the modern era – highly relevant for understanding the city's culture and transformation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kiyosumi-Shirakawa – Tokyo's specialty coffee capital and a trendy creative district. Explore the neighborhood's acclaimed third-wave coffee roasters (Allpress, Blue Bottle Japan's original location, Arise Coffee). Visit the beautiful Kiyosumi Garden (¥150), a traditional strolling garden with large stepping stones across a central pond.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Nihonbashi (15-min walk from Kiyosumi) – one of Tokyo's oldest commercial districts, now blending Edo-era history with modern luxury. Explore the historic Nihonbashi bridge area and enjoy dinner at one of the area's excellent restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel area café (~¥400–¥800)
meals.lunch: Kiyosumi-Shirakawa – a specialty coffee shop lunch or a nearby café with food (~¥1,000–¥1,800)
meals.dinner: Nihonbashi – try Edo-mae sushi at a mid-range sushi counter or a traditional kaiseki-lite restaurant (~¥3,000–¥5,000)

day_by_day.notes: Kiyosumi-Shirakawa is only a 15-min walk from your Tsukiji hotel – a great neighborhood to explore on foot. Kiyosumi Garden is one of Tokyo's most underrated gardens. Check the Edo-Tokyo Museum's renovation status before visiting.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kamakura (about 1 hour from Tokyo by JR Yokosuka Line from Tokyo Station). Visit the Great Buddha (Kotoku-in, ¥300) – a massive 13-meter bronze statue dating from 1252. Explore Kotoku-in temple grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore more of Kamakura – hike the Daibutsu Hiking Trail through bamboo groves and forested hills connecting several temples. Visit Hokokuji Temple (¥300) for its spectacular bamboo grove and traditional matcha tea ceremony in the garden. Browse Kamakura's charming Komachi-dori shopping street.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo in the early evening. Enjoy a relaxed dinner near the hotel in Tsukiji – perhaps try a different style of Japanese cuisine you haven't had yet.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast near Tokyo Station or a convenience store before departure (~¥400–¥800)
meals.lunch: Kamakura – try shirasu (whitebait) rice bowl, a local specialty, at a restaurant near Hase Station (~¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Tsukiji area – try a shabu-shabu or sukiyaki restaurant for a hot pot experience (~¥2,500–¥4,000)

day_by_day.notes: Round-trip JR fare to Kamakura: ~¥1,940. Consider a JR Pass day use if you have one. Kamakura can be crowded on weekends in spring – arrive early. The Daibutsu Hiking Trail takes 1.5–2 hours and involves some steep sections; wear good shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning in the Marunouchi and Imperial Palace area – Tokyo's historic and business heart. Walk the Imperial Palace East Gardens (free, open to public). View the iconic Nijubashi Bridge and the palace moat. Explore the elegant Marunouchi Brick Square and the historic Tokyo Station building (beautiful red-brick architecture).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Akihabara one more time for any remaining tech or souvenir shopping, or head to Nakameguro – a stylish canal-side neighborhood beloved for its boutiques, galleries, and café culture. Walk along the Meguro River (especially beautiful in spring) and browse the independent shops.
day_by_day.evening: Final special dinner evening – splurge slightly on a memorable meal. Consider an omakase sushi experience at a reputable mid-range counter (¥5,000–¥8,000 per person) or a teppanyaki restaurant. Enjoy a final nightcap at a rooftop bar with Tokyo skyline views.

meals.breakfast: A proper Japanese breakfast set at a local restaurant near Tsukiji (~¥800–¥1,500)
meals.lunch: Nakameguro – a stylish café lunch or a popular ramen shop in the area (~¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Mid-range omakase sushi or teppanyaki for a special farewell dinner (~¥5,000–¥8,000)

day_by_day.notes: Imperial Palace East Gardens are closed on Mondays and Fridays. Nakameguro is particularly beautiful in spring with cherry blossom trees lining the canal. Book the farewell dinner restaurant in advance, especially for omakase.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo – take a slow, nostalgic walk through Tsukiji Outer Market one last time for breakfast. Pick up any last-minute food souvenirs: premium green tea, nori seaweed, wasabi, Japanese snacks, or artisan kitchen tools from the nearby Kappabashi area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your flight time: if afternoon/evening departure, pack up and check out of the hotel. Store luggage at the hotel or at a coin locker at Tokyo Station. Do any final shopping at Ginza Six or Coredo Muromachi in Nihonbashi for high-quality Japanese goods and souvenirs. Head to the airport (allow 2–3 hours before departure).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Tokyo. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast – fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and miso soup (~¥1,500–¥2,000)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Tokyo Station's Ramen Street or Ekiben (station bento box) to enjoy on the airport train (~¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Narita Express from Tokyo Station to Narita Airport: ~¥3,070 (30 min to Shinjuku, 80 min total). Allow at least 3 hours before international departure. Redeem any tax-free purchases at the airport. Don't forget to tap out your Suica card and consider keeping it for future visits – it retains its balance.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Tokyo, Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the iconic Tsukiji Outer Market and sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from local vendors. Engage with fishmongers and food artisans who have been operating for generations, offering an authentic taste of Tokyo's legendary food culture.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tokyo airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and arrange private transfer to boutique stay in Tsukiji, Chuo City. Check-in and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely stroll through the Tsukiji Outer Market area to get your bearings. Browse the covered shopping lanes, pick up artisan snacks, and soak in the vibrant atmosphere of one of Tokyo's most iconic food districts. Stop at a renowned knife shop such as Tsukiji Masamoto to admire world-class Japanese kitchen knives.
day_by_day.evening: Ease into Tokyo with a premium omakase dinner at a celebrated Tsukiji-area sushi counter — reserve a seat at Sushi Saito annex or a highly-rated local counter such as Sushi Yoshitake (Ginza, 10 min away) for an intimate chef's tasting experience.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy light refreshments on the flight or at the airport lounge upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick but exceptional bowl of ramen or a fresh sushi set from a top-rated stall in Tsukiji Outer Market upon settling in — try Sushi Dai or Daiwa Sushi for the classic experience.
meals.dinner: Omakase sushi dinner at Sushi Yoshitake (3 Michelin stars, Ginza) or a premium counter in Tsukiji — expect 15–20 courses of the finest seasonal seafood, sake pairing recommended.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally relaxed to combat jet lag. Confirm restaurant reservations well in advance — top omakase counters in Tokyo book out months ahead. Private airport transfer recommended for comfort.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — join an exclusive small-group or private guided tour of the iconic Tsukiji Outer Market. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (rolled omelette), grilled scallops, matcha, and artisan street snacks from legendary vendors. Learn about Tokyo's seafood culture from an expert local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ginza (5 min from Tsukiji) for a world-class luxury shopping and culture experience. Visit the Itoya flagship stationery store (9 floors of premium Japanese design), explore the Ginza Six mall, and pop into the Hermès Maison Ginza building to see the Renzo Piano-designed glass facade. Visit the Ginza Sony Park for a taste of cutting-edge tech installations.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Kabuki performance at the Kabukiza Theatre in Ginza — one of the world's great theatrical experiences. Book a premium box seat for the full immersive cultural experience. Single-act tickets are available if a full program feels long after jet lag.

meals.breakfast: Fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and grilled seafood tastings during the Tsukiji Market Food Tour — a feast in itself.
meals.lunch: Tempura Kondo (Ginza, Michelin-starred) — exquisite seasonal vegetable and seafood tempura in an elegant setting.
meals.dinner: Post-Kabuki dinner at Ginza Kojyu (3 Michelin stars) — refined kaiseki cuisine celebrating the finest seasonal Japanese ingredients.

day_by_day.notes: Book Kabukiza Theatre tickets in advance online. The Tsukiji Outer Market is most vibrant in the morning — starting by 8:00 AM is ideal. Dress smartly for Kabuki and dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Hamarikyu Gardens (10 min walk from Tsukiji) — a stunning feudal-era landscape garden with tidal ponds, teahouses, and seasonal cherry blossoms or spring flowers. Enjoy a traditional matcha tea ceremony in the authentic 300-year-old Nakajima no Ochaya teahouse set on an island in the garden.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board a scenic Tokyo Bay water bus from Hamarikyu to Asakusa, drifting past the Rainbow Bridge and Tokyo Skytree. Arrive in Asakusa and explore the Senso-ji Temple complex — Tokyo's oldest and most spectacular temple. Wander the Nakamise shopping street for premium craft souvenirs, lacquerware, and traditional sweets.
day_by_day.evening: Ascend the Tokyo Skytree (634 m) at dusk for a breathtaking panoramic view of the city as the lights come on. Reserve access to the Tembo Galleria (top deck) for the most exclusive vantage point. Dine at one of the tower's premium restaurants overlooking the illuminated skyline.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or a premium Japanese morning set at a nearby Tsukiji café — miso soup, grilled fish, rice, pickles, and tamagoyaki.
meals.lunch: Asakusa Imahan — legendary sukiyaki and shabu-shabu restaurant near Senso-ji, serving premium Wagyu beef in a traditional setting since 1895.
meals.dinner: Sky Restaurant 634 at Tokyo Skytree or Musashi (Skytree Town) — contemporary Japanese cuisine with an unrivaled Tokyo skyline view.

day_by_day.notes: Hamarikyu Gardens opens at 9:00 AM. Pre-purchase Tokyo Skytree tickets online to skip queues. The water bus journey takes approximately 40 minutes and is a highlight in itself.

day_by_day.morning: Full immersion in Tokyo's tech culture — visit Akihabara Electric Town, Tokyo's legendary electronics and anime district. Explore multi-story electronics megastores (Yodobashi Camera, BIC Camera), retro gaming arcades, and cutting-edge gadget shops. Visit the Akihabara Radio Kaikan for niche tech and collector culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to Odaiba, Tokyo's futuristic artificial island in Tokyo Bay. Visit teamLab Planets or teamLab Borderless (if reopened at new venue) — a world-renowned digital art museum offering a completely immersive, boundary-dissolving experience blending art and technology. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Odaiba waterfront at sunset — enjoy views of the Rainbow Bridge, the life-size Gundam statue, and the glittering Tokyo skyline reflected on the bay. Dine at a premium waterfront restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji area breakfast — fresh oysters, uni (sea urchin), and coffee from a top Outer Market vendor.
meals.lunch: Akihabara lunch at a themed or specialty restaurant — or a quick premium bento from a department store basement food hall (depachika) in nearby Ueno.
meals.dinner: Tableaux (Odaiba) or a premium teppanyaki restaurant on the Odaiba waterfront — Wagyu beef, fresh seafood, and stunning bay views.

day_by_day.notes: teamLab venues require advance ticket booking — check the latest location and availability for 2027. Akihabara is most lively in the afternoon. Odaiba is accessible by the scenic Yurikamome monorail from Shimbashi.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko — board a private or first-class reserved Shinkansen/limited express from Ueno or Asakusa to Nikko (approx. 2 hours). Explore the UNESCO World Heritage Tosho-gu Shrine complex — an extraordinarily ornate mausoleum of Tokugawa Ieyasu set among ancient cedar forests. See the famous 'see no evil, hear no evil, speak no evil' monkeys and the Yomeimon Gate.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko's sacred sites — visit Futarasan Shrine and Rinno-ji Temple. Walk the cedar-lined Cryptomeria Avenue (Nikko Sugi Namiki) for a serene, otherworldly experience. If time allows, take a short taxi to the stunning Kegon Falls and Lake Chuzenji.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Relax and enjoy a quiet, refined dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure to Nikko.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nikko Kanaya Hotel — a historic Victorian-era hotel with a beautiful dining room serving Japanese and Western cuisine; a Nikko institution since 1873.
meals.dinner: Sushi Saito (if reservations secured) or a premium sashimi dinner at a Ginza or Tsukiji counter — celebrate the day's cultural journey.

day_by_day.notes: Nikko is approximately 2 hours from Tokyo. Start early (depart by 7:30–8:00 AM) to maximize time. A private car and guide to Nikko is recommended for the premium experience. Tosho-gu can be crowded on weekends — arrive early.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Yanaka — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) neighborhoods. Wander the atmospheric Yanaka Ginza shopping street, browse antique shops and traditional craft stores, visit the historic Yanaka Cemetery (a tranquil cherry blossom spot), and discover hidden temples and shrines. A rare glimpse of pre-war Tokyo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno (the largest art museum in Japan) — explore its world-class collection of Japanese art, samurai armor, ancient ceramics, Buddhist sculpture, and ukiyo-e woodblock prints. The Honkan (Japanese Gallery) is unmissable. Consider a premium private guided tour for deeper context.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Tokyo's legendary cocktail culture — visit the Bar High Five in Ginza or Star Bar Ginza, consistently ranked among the world's best bars. Master bartenders craft bespoke cocktails using Japanese whisky, rare spirits, and seasonal ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka area breakfast — stop at a traditional kissaten (old-school Japanese coffee shop) for coffee, toast, and a boiled egg.
meals.lunch: Ueno Seiyoken Grill — a historic Western-style restaurant in Ueno Park serving classic Japanese-Western yoshoku cuisine since 1876.
meals.dinner: Quintessential Tokyo ramen experience — visit Fuunji (Shinjuku) or Ivan Ramen for premium tsukemen or shoyu ramen, followed by a nightcap at a rooftop bar.

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes. The Tokyo National Museum is closed on Mondays — check the 2027 calendar and substitute with the National Museum of Western Art or Ueno Zoo if needed. Bar reservations recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Immerse in Harajuku and Omotesando — begin at the serene Meiji Jingu Shrine, set within a 70-hectare forested sanctuary dedicated to Emperor Meiji. Walk the grand gravel path through towering torii gates. Explore the adjacent Yoyogi Park, especially beautiful in spring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll down Omotesando — Tokyo's most elegant boulevard, lined with flagship stores by the world's top luxury brands (Louis Vuitton, Prada, Dior) housed in stunning architecture by Tadao Ando, Herzog & de Meuron, and others. Visit the Omotesando Hills complex and browse the boutiques of Minami-Aoyama for Japanese designer fashion and contemporary art galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Roppongi Art Triangle — visit the Mori Art Museum (stunning city views from the 53rd floor) or the National Art Center. Dine in Roppongi's vibrant upscale dining scene.

meals.breakfast: Premium hotel breakfast or a specialty café breakfast in Omotesando — try Bread, Espresso & (Pan to Espresso to) for exceptional Japanese milk bread and coffee.
meals.lunch: Florilège (Aoyama, 2 Michelin stars) — innovative French-Japanese cuisine using seasonal local ingredients in an open kitchen setting; one of Tokyo's most exciting restaurants.
meals.dinner: Roppongi Hills Club or Inakaya (Roppongi) — a theatrical robatayaki (fireside grilling) experience where chefs grill premium meats, seafood, and vegetables over open charcoal.

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is free to enter and opens at sunrise. Omotesando is best explored in the afternoon when shops are open. Mori Art Museum is open late on Tuesdays — ideal for an evening visit.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day experience in Shinjuku — begin with the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation decks (free, panoramic city views). Explore the surrounding Nishi-Shinjuku skyscraper district — a forest of futuristic towers that defines Tokyo's modern skyline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the contrasts of Shinjuku — visit the tranquil Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (one of Japan's finest, with French, English, and Japanese garden sections). Then plunge into the electric energy of Kabukicho entertainment district and the neon-lit alleys of Golden Gai — a maze of tiny bars, each seating fewer than 10 people.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Golden Gai at night — choose a bar that suits your taste (jazz, film, literature, rock) and enjoy intimate conversation with locals and the bartender. Follow with a premium Wagyu yakiniku dinner.

meals.breakfast: Depachika (department store basement) breakfast experience at Isetan Shinjuku — select premium pastries, Japanese sweets, and specialty coffee from world-class vendors.
meals.lunch: Shinjuku Kappo Nakajima (Michelin-starred) — extraordinary value kaiseki or a premium set lunch of seasonal Japanese cuisine.
meals.dinner: Yakiniku Jumbo Hanare (Shinjuku) — premium A5 Wagyu beef yakiniku in an elegant private room setting; one of Tokyo's finest grilled beef experiences.

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen charges a small entry fee and is closed on Mondays. Golden Gai bars are cash-only and some have cover charges — carry yen. Book the yakiniku restaurant in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Hakone — depart early by Romancecar (luxury express train from Shinjuku, 85 minutes) to Hakone. On a clear day, enjoy iconic views of Mount Fuji across Lake Ashi. Visit Hakone Open Air Museum — a spectacular outdoor sculpture park featuring works by Picasso, Henry Moore, and Japanese masters set against mountain scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Hakone Ropeway over volcanic Owakudani (sulfurous hot spring vents) for dramatic mountain views. Cruise on Lake Ashi aboard a replica pirate ship with Mount Fuji as a backdrop. Visit Hakone Shrine on the lakeshore — a stunning vermillion torii gate rising from the water.
day_by_day.evening: Check in for one night at a premium ryokan (Japanese inn) in Hakone — such as Gora Kadan or Hakone Suishoen — for an authentic onsen (hot spring bath) and kaiseki dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Hakone Open Air Museum café or a local soba restaurant near Gora station.
meals.dinner: Full multi-course kaiseki dinner at the ryokan — a ceremonial procession of seasonal dishes served in your private room, paired with sake and ending with a soak in the private onsen.

day_by_day.notes: Book the ryokan well in advance — Gora Kadan and similar premium properties fill up quickly. The Romancecar should be reserved ahead of time. Check Mount Fuji visibility forecasts — spring can be hazy but April is generally favorable.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up at the Hakone ryokan and enjoy a traditional Japanese breakfast (grilled fish, miso soup, rice, pickles, tofu) served in your room. Take a final morning soak in the onsen before checkout. Explore the Hakone area further — visit the Pola Museum of Art, set in a beech forest, housing an outstanding Impressionist and Japanese art collection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Tokyo by Romancecar. Spend the afternoon exploring Shibuya — visit the iconic Shibuya Scramble Crossing (the world's busiest pedestrian intersection), ascend to the Shibuya Sky observation deck for sweeping 360° city views, and pay respects at the Hachiko statue.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Daikanyama and Nakameguro — Tokyo's coolest neighborhoods. Browse the Daikanyama T-Site (a stunning bookstore and cultural complex), then walk along the Meguro River (lined with cherry trees, magical in spring) and explore the boutiques and restaurants of Nakameguro.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Japanese breakfast at the ryokan — a beautifully presented multi-dish morning feast.
meals.lunch: Soba lunch at a respected Hakone or Odawara restaurant before boarding the Romancecar back to Tokyo.
meals.dinner: Nakameguro dinner at Ryuzu or a premium French-Japanese bistro along the river — intimate atmosphere with excellent seasonal cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Check out of the ryokan by 11:00 AM. Shibuya Sky observation deck tickets should be pre-booked. The Meguro River at night is particularly atmospheric — lined with lanterns and restaurant terraces.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Koenji and Shimokitazawa — Tokyo's bohemian, counter-cultural neighborhoods. Browse vintage clothing stores, independent record shops, and quirky cafés. Visit a live music venue or a specialty coffee roaster. This is a side of Tokyo rarely seen by tourists — authentic, creative, and completely unique.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation) on Odaiba — one of the world's great science and technology museums. See ASIMO the humanoid robot, explore exhibits on artificial intelligence, space exploration, the internet, and the future of humanity. A must for tech culture enthusiasts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Tokyo for a premium whisky tasting experience. Visit the Suntory Whisky Bar or the Hibiki Bar in a luxury hotel — sample rare Japanese single malts, blends, and limited editions guided by an expert whisky sommelier.

meals.breakfast: Specialty coffee and artisan pastry breakfast at a Shimokitazawa or Koenji roaster café.
meals.lunch: Curry lunch at a beloved Shimokitazawa curry house — Japanese curry is an art form, and this neighborhood has some of the city's best.
meals.dinner: Sukiyabashi Jiro Honten (Ginza, if reservations secured — one of the world's most famous sushi restaurants) or a premium alternative omakase counter — a bucket-list dining experience.

day_by_day.notes: Miraikan is closed on Tuesdays and some Wednesdays. Shimokitazawa is best explored on foot. Sukiyabashi Jiro requires reservations made months in advance — arrange through your hotel concierge or a luxury travel service.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive private cooking class with a master chef — learn to prepare authentic Japanese dishes such as dashi broth, miso soup, nigiri sushi, tamagoyaki, and seasonal vegetable dishes. Classes led by a Michelin-level chef or a renowned culinary school (ABC Cooking Studio premium private session or Hattori Nutrition College guest experience).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum in Ryogoku (if open in 2027 after renovations) — an extraordinary museum tracing 400 years of Tokyo's history with life-size reconstructions of Edo-period streets, bridges, and theaters. Alternatively, visit the Sumida Hokusai Museum for an intimate look at the great ukiyo-e master's life and work.
day_by_day.evening: Final luxury shopping evening in Ginza — visit the Mikimoto Pearl flagship, Wako department store, and the Ginza Six rooftop garden. Enjoy a farewell cocktail at the Peter Bar (Park Hotel Tokyo) or the Mandarin Bar (Mandarin Oriental Tokyo) with panoramic city views.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy the ingredients and dishes prepared during the morning cooking class — the best breakfast of the trip.
meals.lunch: Chanko-nabe (sumo wrestlers' hot pot) lunch in Ryogoku — the sumo district of Tokyo, with several authentic chanko restaurants run by retired sumo wrestlers.
meals.dinner: Grand farewell kaiseki dinner at Kichisen (3 Michelin stars) or Kikunoi Tokyo — a deeply moving, multi-course celebration of Japanese culinary philosophy and seasonal beauty.

day_by_day.notes: Book the private cooking class well in advance. The Edo-Tokyo Museum was under renovation — confirm status for 2027. Chanko-nabe is hearty and warming — ideal for a spring evening in Ryogoku.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tsukiji — wake up early for one last visit to the Tsukiji Outer Market. Enjoy a farewell breakfast of the freshest sushi and seafood, buy artisan food souvenirs (premium dashi packets, high-grade matcha, Tsukiji knives, pickled delicacies), and say goodbye to the vendors you've come to know over the past two weeks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time — visit the Hama-rikyu Gardens one final time for a quiet, reflective stroll. Pack and check out of the boutique stay. Arrange private luxury transfer to the airport. Allow ample time for international departure procedures.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Tokyo. Settle into the airport lounge with a glass of Japanese whisky or sparkling sake and reflect on an extraordinary 13-day journey through the food, technology, and culture of one of the world's greatest cities.

meals.breakfast: Final Tsukiji Outer Market feast — premium sushi, tamagoyaki, fresh oysters, and matcha; a perfect full-circle moment from Day 2.
meals.lunch: Light, elegant bento from a Ginza or Tsukiji premium food shop — ideal for a pre-departure meal.
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Narita or Haneda — both airports have exceptional Japanese restaurants; try a premium ramen or sushi counter for a final taste of Japan.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3–4 hours before international departure for check-in and security. Haneda Airport (HND) is closer to central Tokyo than Narita (NRT) — confirm your departure airport. Duty-free shopping at Japanese airports is world-class — budget time for last-minute purchases of cosmetics, whisky, and confectionery.
